text:
maria: APAC GPU nodepool reporting 100% Pending pods, autoscaler not adding nodes. Started ~6m ago after the kubelet rolling upgrade.
jay: Seeing same. Pod status: Pending -> "AttachVolume" sometimes, but a lot show "0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taint that the pod didn't tolerate".
leo: @maria can you paste the event lines? I want to confirm taint name.
maria: kubectl get events -n inference | tail -n 5
```
Normal  PodScheduled     default/my-job-xxx    0/3 nodes are available: 3 node(s) had taint gpu:NoSchedule
Warning FailedScheduling default/async-infer  0/2 nodes are available: 2 node(s) didn't tolerate taint gpu:NoSchedule
```
ops-oncall: autoscaler logs show scale-up requests, but nodes failing registration due to kubelet label/taint mismatch (post-upgrade kubelet now enforces alpha taint syntax). k8s-bot: CA event: "scale-up rejected: NodeGroup taint doesn't match pod toleration".
maria: Confirmed: our node-template uses taint key "gpu" (no prefix) but kubelet upgrade defaulted to "gpu.amazonaws.com/gpu" on new nodes for drivers. Existing nodepools have old taint, new nodes have new key -> pods don't tolerate, CA thinks group incompatible and doesn't attach.
jay: Ouch. So autoscaler is requesting nodes but they come back with incompatible taints causing effectively 0 usable capacity -> scaling storm.
leo: Short-term mitigation: create an emergency nodepool with explicit taint matching the pod toleration and force CA to use it, then cordon/evict problematic nodes.
ops-oncall: Spawning gpu-emergency-ondemand pool (p4d.8x on-demand) with node labels: "workload=inference,gpu=true" and taint key: "gpu" (no prefix). Applying toleration to pods via deployment patch.
maria: Commands run: 
```
# create nodepool (internal tool)
pictl nodepool create --name gpu-emergency-ondemand --instance p4d.8x --size 3 --taint "gpu:NoSchedule" --labels "workload=inference,gpu=true"
kubectl patch deployment inference-api -n prod -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"gpu","operator":"Exists","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}}}'
```
sre-bot: nodepool gpu-emergency-ondemand created, 3 nodes requested.
jay: After pool created, pods started scheduling to it. Rolling capacity up prevented more Pending backlogs. :thumbsup:
leo: Medium-term: we need to normalize taint key usage across nodepool bootstrap configs and update the onboarding doc. Also update CA filter/expander so it doesn't try incompatible groups.
ops-oncall: Cost note: emergency on-demand pool ~+$20k/month at current run rates if left active. I've set an automated TTL to drain and delete in 3 hours unless we flip the flag.
maria: Follow-ups: 1) Backfill a migration plan to reconcile taint keys across our images/init scripts. 2) Add a pre-upgrade validation that checks node-template taint schema. 3) Postmortem scheduled after 12:00 UTC.
jay: Thanks everyone. Leaving some logs here for the postmortem: 
```
/k8s/events grep -i "taint"
autoscaler.log | sed -n '1,200p' | grep "taint"
```
ops-oncall: We'll keep the emergency pool for now, monitoring for CPU/GPU utilization and cost. If no further issues, we'll drain in 2.5h. :alarm_clock:
k8s-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> degraded, monitoring.
